deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen observing journal, May 1818. The weekdays fit 1818: May 3 is a Sunday and May 6 a Wednesday. The reduction epoch '1819' and the 'Pond 1815' catalogue on the previous page fix the year. The page has two parts: (A) a latitude determination from the meridian zenith distance of alpha Virginis (Spica), continuing the alpha Hydrae work on the previous page; (B) the May 6 observations of the level, Sirius and Castor, used for clock correction and zenith distances.

(A) SPICA

A1. Refraction (top logs). Gauss adds
- 2.03040 = log of the mean refraction, 107.26";
- 0.00305, probably the barometer factor;
- 9.99545, probably the thermometer factor.
The sum 2.02890 gives r = 106.88". [Check, mine: 57.7" tan 61.7° ≈ 107".]

A2. Precession. 18.98 is the annual precession in declination for Spica, 20.05" |cos alpha| with alpha ≈ 199°. 0.03 is a proper-motion term. Together 19.01"/yr, and log 19.01 = 1.27898.
- Subtracting log 365.25 = 2.56259 gives 8.71639 = log of the daily rate.
- Adding log 243.8 = 2.38696 (days from May 1 to 1819.0) gives 12.69".
- Adding log 213.8 = 2.33009 (days from May 31) gives 11.13".
- The intermediate values 12.17 and 11.65 are linear, in steps of 0.52.

A3. Table of reductions 'vom May 1–31', tabulated at May 1, 11, 21, 31. Each term is the correction delta_mean(1819.0) − delta_apparent.
- Aberration: h sin(lambda_sun + H), with log h = 0.8845 (h = 7.66") and H = 63°42'. The Sun's longitudes are 40°52', 50°31', 60°7', 69°41' (degree.minute notation). The log sines 9.9858, 9.9600, 9.9195, 9.8614 give +7.42, +6.99, +6.37, +5.57.
- Lunar nutation: g sin(Omega + G), with log g = 0.8738 (g = 7.48") and G = 155°17'. The Moon's node Omega runs from 38°43' to 37°8'. The log sines 9.3837n … 9.3325n give −1.81, −1.74, −1.68, −1.61.
- Solar (semi-annual) nutation: k sin(2 lambda + 160°), with log k = 9.658 (k = 0.455"). Here 2 lambda = 81°44', 101°2', 120°14', 139°22'. The log sines 9.945n, 9.995n, 9.993n, 9.940n give −0.40, −0.45, −0.45, −0.40.
- Precession to 1819.0: −12.69, −12.17, −11.65, −11.13.
- Sums: −7.48, −7.37, −7.41, −7.57.

A4. Theory check (mine). For alpha ≈ 198.96°, delta ≈ −10.21°, epsilon ≈ 23.46° and constant 20.25":
- Aberration in declination is −20.25[0.3389 cos lambda + 0.1677 sin lambda] = −7.66 cos(lambda − 26°20'). Its negative is 7.66 sin(lambda + 63°40'), matching Gauss's h and H.
- The lunar-nutation phase 155°17' matches. The amplitude 7.48 implies about 18.0" in longitude and 9.6" in obliquity. These are pre-Bessel constants, not the later 17.25/9.25.
- The solar-nutation phase 160° also matches.

A5. Latitude. For a star south of the zenith, z = phi − delta, so z_mean = z_app + (delta_app − delta_mean) = z_app + 7.48. Two lines are worked:
- First line (May 1, using the May 1 reduction 7.48): observed z = 61°42'59.76"; plus refraction 106.88" gives 61°44'46.64"; plus 7.48" gives 61°44'54.12" (mean, 1819.0).
- Mean declination: Pond 1815 gives −10°11'29.40"; four years of precession, 76.08", give −10°12'45.48" for 1819.0.
- Hence phi = 61°44'54.12" − 10°12'45.48" = 51°32'8.64". The '!' marks disagreement with alpha Hydrae (51°31'12.63", previous page).
- May 8: 61°43'7.95" + 104.61" = 61°44'52.56"; plus 7.40" (interpolated for May 8) gives 61°44'59.96". Hence phi = 51°32'14.48".

(B) MAY 6

B1. Level (Libelle): two sets of readings, the second after wiping ('abgewischt'). Pairwise means: 3'20.25", 3'29.8", 3'12.075".

B2. Sirius, transit times.
- Wire times 6h36'46.6", 6h37'3.9", 6h37'20.8" have mean 6h37'3.77".
- Tabulated right ascension 6h37'6.798"; correction 0.067 applied with negative sign gives 6.731".
- Clock correction 3.77 − 6.731 = −2.96 s.

B3. Sirius, zenith distance.
- Circle 68°1'43.0", microscopes 1'56.2", 1'32.7". Barometer 27 in 2.25 lines; thermometers 12.5° and 11.5°.
- Refraction factors 9.99695 (thermometer?) + 9.98722 (barometer; 27"2.25''' / 28" = 0.971) = 9.98417.
- 2.15293 is the log mean refraction (142.2"); the true refraction is 10^(2.15293 + 9.98417 − 10) ≈ 137.1" (my completion).
- Reduced reading 67°58'23.42"; the correction from the raw reading is not reconstructible with certainty.

B4. Castor, transit times.
- Wire times 22'35.9", 22'54.9", 23'14.2" have mean 7h22'55.00".
- Right ascension 7h22'57.268" + 0.551 = 57.82".
- Clock correction −2.82 s.

B5. Castor, zenith distance.
- Circle 19°18'26.3", microscopes 3'37.4", 3'16.7"; barometer 27"2.25'''; thermometers 12.4°, 11.7°.
- Log factors 9.99653 + 9.98722 = 9.98375; log mean refraction 1.30535 (20.20").
- Refraction 19.46"; 19°15'6.11" + 19.46" = 19°15'25.57".
errors: Minor: the 4-year precession 76.08" is slightly more than 4×19.01 = 76.04"; possibly a secular term was included, or a small slip.
Sirius: the correction is written '0,067' without a sign but is subtracted (6.798 − 0.067 = 6.731), while Castor's +0.551 is added. Not an error, but the sign is implicit.

Not a computational error: the two Spica latitudes (51°32'8.6", 51°32'14.5") differ by about 1' from alpha Hydrae (51°31'12.6"). The modern value is about 51°31'48", which is roughly the mean, pointing to an uncorrected zenith-point or flexure error. Gauss flags the discrepancy with '!'.
All other additions, subtractions, log sums and table sums check to the last digit (e.g. 7.42 − 1.81 − 0.40 − 12.69 = −7.48).

results.what: Reduction of apparent to mean declination (1819.0) of Spica: precession, annual aberration (h sin(lambda+H)), lunar nutation (g sin(Omega+G)), solar nutation (k sin(2lambda+G'))
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration, nutation), Lalande, von Zach, Delambre tables; standard form by Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830)

results.what: Refraction as mean refraction times barometer and thermometer factors (log form)
Latitude of Göttingen from the meridian zenith distance of a star of known declination: phi = z + delta
Clock correction from mean of wire transit times minus apparent right ascension (Sirius −2.96 s, Castor −2.82 s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observing-journal page from Gauss's Göttingen observatory work (1818). It contains standard reductions for refraction, precession, aberration and nutation, using contemporary constants, plus clock corrections and latitude. Gauss's astronomical and latitude work at Göttingen is well documented; nothing here is mathematically novel.

transcription_corrections: First solar-nutation log (row May 1) is 9.945n (overwritten in the image), not 9.995n; it is required for the value −0.40.
Castor's first refraction log should be 9.99653 (9.98375 − 9.98722), not '9.9657'.
'60.7' and the other first-column values are degrees.minutes (60°7'), Sun's longitudes; '81.44' etc. are 2·lambda in degrees.minutes.
Fourth precession entry is −11.65 (confirmed by the 0.52 steps and the row sum).
'27 2 2'25' / '27. 2,25' means barometer 27 Paris inches 2.25 lines; '12°5 11°5' are the attached and outside thermometers.
'Mittg' over 10.12.45.48 most likely abbreviates 'Mittl.' (mean declination) rather than 'Mittag'.
Libelle second-row third value is 3'9"25 (3'9.25"); the third mean is 3'12.075".
The Sirius correction 0,067 is applied negatively (6.798 → 6.731).
